::: {.why}
Reasoning about quoting is not the same as quoting under time pressure against an adversary, and a simulator with real competition data is the closest free substitute for the real round.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Run a market-making strategy in the Prosperity backtester and report its profit and its inventory profile.
- Say which of your losses came from adverse selection and which from inventory risk.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Write a simple market maker for one product: quote symmetrically around a fair value estimate, skew against inventory, and widen when recent flow has been one-sided. That is your day 25 simulation with a real counterparty, and the parameters you chose there are the ones to start from.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Attribute the outcome rather than only reporting it: split profit into spread captured, inventory profit and loss, and adverse selection measured as the mid drift after your fills. The attribution is the useful output and it is exactly the day 284 decomposition applied to your own quotes.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A market-making strategy running in the backtester with profit attributed across spread, inventory and adverse selection.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your market maker lost money. Was it adverse selection or inventory, and what number told you?
:::
